title: Dong-okjeo
capsule: Dong-okjeo (Eastern Okjeo; 옥저) was a small tribal polity occupying the coastal lowlands of the northeastern Korean peninsula, roughly corresponding to the modern Hamgyŏng provinces of North Korea, attested from the late first century BCE. It lacked a centralized state structure and paid tribute first to the Han commandery of Xuantu and later to Goguryeo, which absorbed it by the mid-second century CE. Chinese dynastic histories—the Sanguo zhi and Hou Han shu—record Dong-okjeo as distinct from western (Xi-)Okjeo and note its population's maritime subsistence economy centered on fishing and salt production.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Spatial extent is inferred from Chinese commandery records and archaeology; precise boundaries are uncertain and subject to ongoing debate among Korean and Chinese historians.
